topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: Ran into an old face today, or so I thought. Corner café, smudged with rain, the kind of place where memories ought to stick but don’t. She looked through me like I was yesterday’s news, flat and done. Asked her about the times, the laughs, the secrets we thought were forever. Blank stare, colder than the leftover coffee in my cup. Maybe time really does wash away the shores, or maybe it just picks and chooses what to keep. I tried to jog her memory, but you can’t force a lost puzzle piece back in. Dug deep for a smile, a flash of recognition, but the rain kept falling and the streets swirled with faceless faces. Some bonds, I guess, are just rented, not bought. Left the café, left the rain, but the chill won’t leave my bones.
